clue.text: Member of The Police responsible for the beat?

definitions.text: Member of The Police responsible for the beat?

parts.words: Member of The Police responsible for the beat
parts.note: reads like the drummer of the rock band The Police, who keeps the beat; really a police officer who walks a beat on foot

explanation.surface: A pop trivia question about which member of the band The Police kept the rhythm.
explanation.walkthrough: The capitalised 'The Police' points to the band and Stewart Copeland on drums; a beat is also the area a constable patrols on foot.
explanation.definitionFit: Flatfoot is old slang for a patrolling policeman, the constable who pounds the streets.

clue.text: Eruptions in trousers you quietly covered up

indicators.note: covered up means the trousers wrap around the letters inside

parts.note: flares are bell-bottom trousers
U stands for you, as in text speak
P is piano, the musical direction for quietly

explanation.surface: An embarrassing outbreak in someone's trousers that is hushed up.
explanation.definitionFit: Flare-ups are sudden outbursts, of fire, temper or illness, which are eruptions.

clue.text: What helps one get a job interview is diligence

definitions.text: What helps one get a job interview
definitions.meaning: the form or letter sent to an employer

explanation.surface: Career advice: hard work is what lands you an interview.
explanation.definitionFit: Sending an application wins the interview, and applying oneself is steady hard work.

clue.text: Excited fans like soprano's eccentricity

indicators.note: excited means stirred up, so the letters of fans and like are rearranged together

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for soprano

explanation.surface: Thrilled admirers relish a singer's quirky behaviour.
explanation.definitionFit: Flakiness is informal for being odd or unreliable, so it suits strange behaviour.

clue.text: Old and wicked character from Greece

parts.note: wicked and mega are both slang for excellent

explanation.surface: An evil villain from ancient Greece.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wicked' reads as evil; it is youth slang for brilliant, as is mega.
explanation.definitionFit: Omega is the last letter of the Greek alphabet, and a letter is a character.

clue.text: A plank on the Queen Anne's Revenge?

definitions.note: an example: being on Blackbeard's ship means being on board a vessel

parts.note: a plank is a board

explanation.surface: Pirate lore: a plank on Blackbeard's ship, presumably for walking.
explanation.walkthrough: The Queen Anne's Revenge was the pirate Blackbeard's flagship; the question mark marks the definition as one example of being on a ship.
explanation.definitionFit: Anyone standing on a particular ship is on board it, so the ship's name stands in for any vessel.

clue.text: Tasteless debut of Love divides musical group

indicators.note: divides means that letter splits the band's letters

parts.note: a band is a musical group

indicators.note: debut is a first appearance, so the first letter of Love

explanation.surface: A dull first album, Love, splits a band's fans.
explanation.definitionFit: Bland food lacks flavour, so it is tasteless.

clue.text: Excellent to drink medium-sized Bud in Paris

indicators.note: to drink means the letters for excellent take in the size letter

parts.note: A1 means first-class; the 1 is read as the letter I
M is the clothing size medium

explanation.surface: A recommendation to drink a medium-sized Budweiser in Paris.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bud' reads as the beer brand; it is American slang for buddy, and the French for friend is ami.
explanation.definitionFit: Ami is French for friend, and bud is a casual word for a friend.

clue.text: One who gives party outside beside river

indicators.note: outside means the party's letters sit around the letters for beside

parts.note: a do is a party
on can mean beside, as in a house on the river

explanation.surface: A generous person hosting a party outdoors by the river.
explanation.definitionFit: A donor makes a gift, of money, blood or organs, so is someone who gives.

clue.text: Bishop getting Australian Dame a drink

parts.note: B is the chess abbreviation for bishop
Dame Edna Everage was Barry Humphries's Australian comic character

explanation.surface: A churchman buys an Australian dame a drink.
explanation.definitionFit: A beverage is any drink other than water, a formal word for something to drink.

clue.text: Dead fast going around end of course

indicators.note: going around says the phrase for fast is wrapped about the next letter

parts.note: going at pace means going fast

indicators.note: end of picks out the final letter of the word course

explanation.surface: Something quick circling the last part of a racecourse, with 'Dead' adding a grim twist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dead fast' looks like one phrase meaning very fast; 'Dead' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Being at peace is a gentle euphemism for having died, as in rest in peace.

clue.text: Relative ignoring Republican in high spirits

indicators.note: ignoring means leaving out the letter for Republican from the word for relative

parts.note: a relative is a relation

explanation.surface: A family member who disregards a Republican and is cheerful about it.
explanation.definitionFit: Elation is great joy; someone in high spirits is in a state of elation, so the phrase names that mood.

clue.text: Priest minister had to do away with?

parts.note: Eli is the priest who raised Samuel in the Bible
MIN is the abbreviation for minister or ministry
had, as in had a meal, means ate

explanation.surface: A priest asks what a government minister had to get rid of.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark covers 'had to' reading as obligation; 'had' is ATE and 'to' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To eliminate something is to get rid of it entirely, the same sense as doing away with it.

clue.text: One spotted around new restaurant primarily?

definitions.text: One spotted around new restaurant primarily?

indicators.note: around says the die's letters are wrapped about the letter for new

parts.note: a die is a cube marked with spots

indicators.note: primarily picks out the first letter of the word restaurant

explanation.surface: A customer seen around a new eatery, mostly.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue also defines: a diner is someone spotted in a restaurant, and the answer is itself a kind of restaurant.
explanation.definitionFit: A diner is someone eating a meal, the sort of person you see at a restaurant table.

clue.text: Patriot Italians not in need of revolution

indicators.note: a revolution overturns things, so the letters of Italians not are rearranged

explanation.surface: A patriot complaining that Italians do not need an uprising.
explanation.definitionFit: A nationalist is fiercely devoted to their own nation, a kind of patriot.

clue.text: Jet in exercises over city close to Brighton

indicators.note: over here means covering, so the letters for exercises go around the rest

parts.note: PE is physical education, school exercises
LA is Los Angeles

indicators.note: close to picks out the final letter of the word Brighton

explanation.surface: A jet aircraft involved in training exercises above a city near Brighton.
explanation.definitionFit: A jet is an aircraft, and a plane is the everyday word for one.

clue.text: Beastly types make a mess of cabarets

indicators.note: making a mess of something jumbles it, so the letters of cabarets are rearranged

explanation.surface: Unruly people who wreck nightclub shows.
explanation.definitionFit: Bearcats are animals, the binturong or red panda, so they are literally beasts.

clue.text: Kids of the 1950s stealing large knickers

indicators.note: stealing means the boomers take the letter for large into themselves

parts.note: baby boomers were born in the post-war baby boom, so were children in the 1950s

explanation.surface: Post-war children pinching oversized underwear.
explanation.definitionFit: Bloomers are loose, knee-length women's knickers, named after Amelia Bloomer.

clue.text: Have a go at conservative criminal agitates

indicators.note: criminal suggests something crooked, so the letters of agitates are rearranged

explanation.surface: A Tory attacking a law-breaking activist.
explanation.definitionFit: To castigate is to rebuke severely, and to have a go at someone is British slang for scolding them.

clue.text: Adult getting short, beautiful woman a flower

parts.note: adult, as in adult films, means risque, which is blue

indicators.note: short means the word for a beautiful woman loses its last letter

parts.note: a belle is a beautiful woman

explanation.surface: A grown-up and a short, pretty woman, then a flower.
explanation.definitionFit: The bluebell is a spring woodland flower with blue, bell-shaped blooms.

clue.text: Large city? That might describe Havana!

definitions.meaning: a nickname for London, or any large city

explanation.surface: A puzzle about Cuba's capital as a large city.
explanation.walkthrough: Havana looks like the city, matching 'Large city'; here it is the cigar named after it.
explanation.definitionFit: London's old nickname comes from its coal smog; a fat cigar is literally a big thing to smoke.

clue.text: Spirit picked up in a foreign capital

indicators.note: picked up, as a radio signal is, means heard, so the word is taken by sound

parts.note: the spirit is the soul

explanation.surface: A ghost caught on tape in an overseas capital.
explanation.definitionFit: Seoul is the capital city of South Korea, a capital outside Britain.

clue.text: Some sot on Galliano is a state

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A drunk on the Italian liqueur Galliano is in quite a state.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is a state' reads as being drunk; 'is' is a link and Tonga is a country.
explanation.definitionFit: Tonga is a sovereign Pacific kingdom, a state in the sense of a nation.

clue.text: Jazz fan upset by The X-Factor is silent

indicators.note: upset in a down clue means turned over, so the word for jazz fan is read backwards

parts.note: a cat is jazz slang for an enthusiast
it means sex appeal or star quality, the elusive X-factor

explanation.surface: A jazz lover dismayed by the TV talent show The X Factor goes quiet.
explanation.definitionFit: Tacit means understood without being said, so unspoken or silent.

clue.text: A jerk holding tenor in a storage space

indicators.note: holding means the word for jerk contains the letter for tenor

parts.note: a tic is an involuntary twitch or jerk

explanation.surface: An idiot keeping a singer locked in a cupboard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'jerk' reads as a fool; it is a sudden twitch.
explanation.definitionFit: An attic is the room under a roof, often used for keeping stored things.

clue.text: I'm a cheat about to wrap up northern plot

indicators.note: to wrap up means the rearranged letters enclose the letter for northern
about means in disorder, so the letters of I'm a cheat are rearranged

explanation.surface: A confession: I am a cheat about to finish off a northern scheme.
explanation.definitionFit: To machinate is to scheme or contrive, which is what plotting means as a verb.

clue.text: One weeping about queen that's on run

parts.note: C is circa, Latin for about
R is regina, queen
i.e. stands for id est, that is
R is the cricket abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: Someone in tears about a queen who has fled.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'on' says the letters for that's sit above the run's letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A crier is someone who cries, which means weeps.

clue.text: Gas milliner gets after drop of Coca-Cola

indicators.note: gets after places the word for milliner behind the opening letter
a drop of a drink is a small amount, here its first letter

parts.note: a milliner makes hats, a hatter

explanation.surface: A hat-maker going for a fizzy cola drink, with gas from the bubbles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gas' is a British informal word for idle talk, not fizz.
explanation.definitionFit: To gas is to talk at length about nothing much, which is to chatter.

clue.text: Beer in cut-price event? Heading off!

indicators.note: heading off means the word for cut-price event loses its first letter

parts.note: a sale is an event with reduced prices

explanation.surface: Is there beer at the bargain sale? Then off we go!
explanation.definitionFit: Ale is a type of beer, brewed with top-fermenting yeast.

clue.text: Picture that's about mother and her ruin?

indicators.note: about means the letters for that's go round the rest

parts.note: i.e. stands for id est, that is
MA is mother
gin is known as mother's ruin, so her ruin, the mother's, is gin

explanation.surface: An image of a mother brought low, with the question hinting at her downfall.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mother's ruin' is a British nickname for gin; 'her' in the clue refers back to the mother.
explanation.definitionFit: To picture something is to form it in the mind, to imagine it.

clue.text: Swimmer crossing end of river channel

indicators.note: crossing means the fish's letters span the letter taken from river

parts.note: a tench is a freshwater fish, a swimmer

indicators.note: end of picks out the final letter of the word river

explanation.surface: Someone swimming across where a river meets the sea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'channel' tempts one toward the English Channel and swimming; here it is a dug ditch.
explanation.definitionFit: A trench is a long narrow ditch, the same as a channel cut into the ground.

clue.text: Awful tailor dressing nurse from the east?

indicators.note: dressing means the rearranged letters clothe the nurse's letters
awful suggests a botched job, so the letters of tailor are rearranged

parts.note: EN is an enrolled nurse

explanation.surface: A dreadful tailor fitting out a nurse who came from Asia.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dressing' fits the tailor in the surface but signals one piece going around another.
explanation.definitionFit: Oriental describes things of the Orient, the eastern lands of Asia.
